title: Resilience sprint retro & hotfix coordination - BlueHarbor postmortem
summary: Short retro after the 2025-10-30 production regression where ~3-6% of BlueHarbor inference requests returned misaligned completions after an autoscale + quantization rollout. We validated the root cause as a race between fast-scale model shard reloads and prefix-cache alignment logic when the quantized kernel path changed. Discussed hotfix deployment cadence, rollback & fail-open controls, longer-term hardened canary procedures, and changes to the autoscaler ramp settings. Agreed on a two-week resilience sprint with specific owners.
topics: Root cause: cache alignment + quantization mismatch
Immediate hotfix plan and rollback criteria
next_steps: Redwood to share micro-rollout checklist and hotfix branch by 2025-11-04
BlueHarbor to provide failing request ids and tenant list by 2025-11-05
Schedule a pair-debug session (SE + BlueHarbor SRE) for 2025-11-06
Finalize resilience sprint backlog and owners by 2025-11-07
action_items: Anil Kapoor: prepare hotfix (faster prefix-align on reload) and branch; due 2025-11-04
Elliot Ramos: export sample error traces and tenant IDs; due 2025-11-05
Priya Patel: draft customer-facing incident timeline & mitigations; due 2025-11-05
Maya Chen: coordinate contract waiver for extended debug hours; due 2025-11-07
Rina Sato: provision staging cluster with BlueHarbor traffic pattern; due 2025-11-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-03 16:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (scheduled 60)
Attendees: Maya, Anil, Priya (Redwood); Elliot, Dana, Tom, Rina, Omar (BlueHarbor)
---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for squeezing this in. We wanted to run through the postmortem, align on the hotfix and owners. Priya is on notes.
[00:18] Priya Patel: Hi all, taking notes. Quick ask, can folks state roles so we map owners?
[00:25] Tom Keating: Tom, CTO. Elliot is SRE lead, Dana runs ML infra, Rina in platform.
[00:33] Anil Kapoor: Perfect. I'll kick off with our timeline reconstruction, and then we can go into the code-level cause.
[00:40] Anil Kapoor: On 2025-10-30 at 03:12 UTC we saw a small spike in error rate on the quantized model pool when BlueHarbor traffic surged due to batch jobs. Autoscaler spun up additional serving hosts, the rollout of quantized kernel v2 began, and around 03:15 we observed 3 to 6 percent of requests returning an obvious truncation/misaligned tokens pattern.
[01:05] Elliot Ramos: Right — from our logs it looked like certain tenants would get responses with injected partial prompts, like tokens repeating from prior request. It was intermittent, not a full outage.
[01:23] Dana Liu: We tried to repro locally but only saw it under high-concurrency synthetic load, which made me suspect a race.
[01:31] Anil Kapoor: Exactly. Our postmortem points to a race during model shard reload: when the quantization path changed, the prefix-cache alignment step (which ties KV positions to the new kernel layout) sometimes ran after the worker started serving new requests, leaving mismatched KV references for a short window.
[01:55] Rina Sato: To be clear, this was only on hosts that got both a kernel change and immediate traffic; warm hosts with no reload were fine.
[02:03] Anil Kapoor: Yep. The code guard existed but the guard was optimistic: it checked in-memory version but didn't block the very first inbound request exactly at handoff.
[02:12] Omar Nazir: How many tenants were impacted? We saw 12 tenant ids in our initial report.
[02:18] Elliot Ramos: We saw about 8 tenants with repeated failures and 4 with single-incident traces; overall roughly 3% of total requests in that window.
[02:25] Maya Chen: From an SLA perspective, you were still within uptime, but we understand this is unacceptable for those affected. We're treating it as a reliability incident.
[02:35] Tom Keating: We want to avoid root causes that are subtle race windows. What's the short-term mitigation? A rollback? A patch?
[02:42] Anil Kapoor: Short-term we have two options: rollback to previous kernel (safe), or a hotfix that makes model reloads block new request handling until prefix alignment completes (fast and targeted). Rollback has the advantage of quick revert but it incurs throttling on perf improvements we shipped.
[03:02] Dana Liu: If the hotfix is small and tested, we prefer that route. We need guarantees about no regression in latency.
[03:10] Anil Kapoor: Understood. The hotfix is essentially a micro-change: add a transient gating on accept loop during reload that ensures KV/prefix alignment completes. Test coverage is small but we'll run regression on sequences and perf microbenchmarks.
[03:28] Priya Patel: We'll want a canary plan that exercises the fast path: customer-specific traffic, high-concurrency, and quantized kernel.
[03:35] Maya Chen: What about autoscaler behavior? The autoscaler spawned hosts too quickly; do we add ramp limits?
[03:40] Elliot Ramos: We saw the group scale from 4 to 12 instances in under 90s. That was aggressive.
[03:47] Anil Kapoor: For immediate mitigation, we can proposal two autoscaler adjustments: increase scale-in/scale-out cool-down to 3 minutes and rate-limit the number of hosts added per interval to 2. Also consider starting new hosts in drained state for a few seconds to let model init finish.
[04:08] Rina Sato: Draining on init might be fine but we need to make sure it doesn't blow cost targets. We can balance shorter drain vs. larger over-provision.
[04:18] Dana Liu: Also worth noting: quantization v2 changed the KV layout slightly; while logically compatible, the mapping offsets differ by a constant. The caching alignment must run post-kernel-init.
[04:33] Anil Kapoor: Yes that's the subtlety — it's not corruption, it's mis-interpretation of the same offsets under a different kernel layout. The temporary mismap gives stale token spelunking.
[04:46] Tom Keating: Good phrasing, "temporary mismap". So next steps are hotfix + canary + autoscaler tweak. Who owns what?
[04:55] Maya Chen: I'll coordinate approvals and extended hours if needed. Priya will handle comms. Anil will lead the hotfix. Elliot/Rina will provide traces and help with canary traffic in staging.
[05:08] Anil Kapoor: Timeline proposal: hotfix branch by 2025-11-04, internal perf smoke by 11-04 afternoon, cautious canary to 5% traffic on 11-05, escalate to full roll on 11-06 if metrics good.
[05:24] Elliot Ramos: We can do 5% on 11-05 but want rollback to be automated and immediate.
[05:31] Anil Kapoor: We'll add an automated rollback policy tied to error-rate + token-alignment mismatch metric.
[05:38] Omar Nazir: What monitoring signals should we tune? We had fuzzy alerts — too many false positives.
[05:44] Priya Patel: Actionable signals proposed: token-alignment-mismatch-rate (derived event), per-tenant error spike, KV-mismatch log signatures, and elevated tail-latency for quantized path. We'll draft thresholds.
[05:58] Dana Liu: Also, can we get a telemetry hook that logs the model-layout-version and prefix-cache-checksum during init? That would help future forensics.
[06:06] Anil Kapoor: Yes we can emit a compact checksum event on successful alignment; that will help correlate.
[06:11] Tom Keating: Any legal/compliance impact? BlueHarbor handles sensitive PII — was any data exfiltrated or persisted incorrectly?
[06:19] Maya Chen: Per our review, this issue manifested in generated outputs only — not data leak. We have no evidence of data being written to unexpected stores. We'll include this statement in the public timeline.
[06:30] Rina Sato: Good. For the resilience sprint, we want prioritized backlog items: (1) harden reload gating, (2) tighter canary plan, (3) autoscaler cool-down policy, (4) richer telemetry, (5) test harness for race windows.
[06:46] Anil Kapoor: We'll add unit/integration tests that simulate concurrent reload + inbound request sequences. Also fuzz tests for kernel layout mismatches.
[06:54] Priya Patel: Customer comms — we'll share an incident timeline with affected tenant ids redacted and a statement of mitigations. Draft ready by 11-05.
[07:03] Maya Chen: On resourcing, we propose a two-week resilience sprint with a small pod: Anil (SE), Rina (BlueHarbor platform), Elliot (SRE), plus one Redwood infra engineer to help with autoscaler changes.
[07:18] Elliot Ramos: Agree. We also want to formalize an emergency on-call ladder for hot patches.
[07:25] Tom Keating: Good idea. We'll share our rotation and we'll sync with Redwood on out-of-hours escalation.
[07:32] Anil Kapoor: Quick question from my side: did you see any correlation with tenant model variants or prompt lengths?
[07:39] Dana Liu: Mostly higher concurrency and larger prefix lengths triggered it more frequently; certain tenant prompt patterns exacerbate misalignment, yes.
[07:47] Anil Kapoor: Makes sense. We'll include that in the canary criteria.
[07:52] Priya Patel: I have a note: Maya, action on contract waiver. Also, Anil, make sure the hotfix branch is small and easy to rollback.
[07:59] Maya Chen: Confirmed.
[08:02] [12:30 remaining] Anil Kapoor: I'll briefly run through the hotfix code plan: one boolean gating flag in the accept loop, a short blocking path during init, and an invariant check that validates prefix-checksum before flipping the host to ready. We also add a lightweight metric.
[08:22] Rina Sato: Please keep the blocking to under 300ms average so it doesn't add startup tail-latency.
[08:28] Anil Kapoor: Yep — measure and tune.
[08:30] Elliot Ramos: For the canary, we prefer traffic from two lower-risk tenants first to validate, then open it to more production traffic.
[08:39] Anil Kapoor: We'll do a staged rollout: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> full, with 15-minute observation windows. Automated rollback triggers on >0.5% token-alignment mismatches or >2x error rate.
[08:55] Tom Keating: That seems conservative enough.
[08:59] Priya Patel: Anything else on the timeline?
[09:02] Maya Chen: No, just to reiterate: hotfix branch 11-04, canary 11-05, ramp 11-06 if green. Customer comms 11-05. Resilience sprint kickoff 11-07.
[09:14] Omar Nazir: Will Redwood share the micro-rollout checklist now?
[09:17] Anil Kapoor: I'll share a checklist link in the follow-up email — it includes pre-checks, monitoring dashboards, rollback commands, and contact on-call.
[09:28] Dana Liu: One last ask: could Redwood run a short loadtest that mirrors our nightly batch to validate the fix? We can supply the batch profile.
[09:36] Anil Kapoor: Absolutely — we can run it in staging with the provided profile.
[09:40] Priya Patel: I'll capture that as an action.
[09:44] Maya Chen: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll close with the recap and action items in the notes.
[09:50] Tom Keating: Thanks all.
[09:53] [END]
